title: MTEL Physical Education (22) Practice Test - MTEL - Nutrition and Health
subject: MTEL

questions.q: Which of the following is a recommended nutritional practice to promote optimal growth and development in young children?
options: including foods that contain more fats than protein in daily meals to promote increased energy stores
consuming three moderately large meals and avoiding or limiting snacks and treats to promote desirable eating patterns
including foods that contain more fiber than fat in daily meals to promote healthy digestive functions
consuming several small meals and snacks of mixed carbohydrates, proteins, and fats each day to promote variety in eating
questions.explain: A balanced intake of carbohydrates, proteins, and fats is crucial for a child's growth. Eating several small meals and snacks helps stabilize energy levels and fosters healthy lifelong dietary habits.
questions.subject: MTEL

questions.q: In recent decades, rates of physical activity among U.S. children and adolescents have declined while rates of sedentary activity and poor dietary practices have increased. Among U.S. youth, this trend has led to a dramatic rise in:
options: the incidence of obesity-related diseases.
visits to hospital emergency rooms due to injuries sustained at home.
the prevalence of vitamin-deficiency diseases.
the occurrence of sleep disorders and fatigue-related ailments.
questions.explain: The combination of decreased physical activity and poor diet has led to a significant increase in childhood obesity. This in turn has caused a dramatic rise in obesity-related diseases, such as type 2 diabetes and cardiovascular disorders.

questions.q: Which of the following health risks is most closely associated with inactivity and a poor fitness level?
options: migraine headaches
high blood pressure
susceptibility to infection
nerve degeneration
questions.explain: Inactivity and poor fitness levels are major risk factors for cardiovascular problems. High blood pressure (hypertension) is a very common negative adaptation of the cardiovascular system to a sedentary lifestyle.

questions.q: Exercise is generally an important part of treatment plans for people with diabetes because physical activity helps:
options: protect the insulin-producing cells of the pancreas.
reduce the build-up of glucose in the blood.
eliminate urinary problems associated with diabetes.
prevent diabetes-induced changes in vision.
questions.explain: In type 2 diabetes, cells become resistant to insulin. Physical activity improves the body's insulin sensitivity, allowing cells to uptake and use glucose from the blood more effectively, thus helping to reduce high blood glucose levels.
questions.subject: MTEL

questions.q: Which of the following best describes two major functions of carbohydrates in the body?
options: controlling fluid levels and ridding the body of wastes
repairing damaged cells and creating new ones
providing energy for cells and maintaining an energy reserve
regulating body temperature and controlling blood sugar
questions.explain: Carbohydrates are the body's primary source of energy. Glucose, derived from carbohydrates, fuels most cellular functions. Excess carbohydrates can be stored (as glycogen or fat) to serve as an energy reserve for later use.

questions.q: Which of the following nutritional areas should be of particular concern for children aged 9 to 14 years because of the bone growth and development that occurs in this age range?
options: adequate fiber intake
adequate carbohydrate intake
adequate fat intake
adequate calcium intake
questions.explain: The 9-14 age range is a critical period for bone growth and development, as peak bone mass is being established. Ensuring adequate calcium intake is essential for building strong, healthy bones during this preadolescent and adolescent stage.
questions.subject: MTEL

questions.q: Body composition is a component of health-related fitness concerned primarily with the:
options: absorption and use of nutrients by the body.
ability of the skeletal system to give shape to the body.
maintenance of bone mass in the body.
relative proportions of fat and lean tissue in the body.
questions.explain: Body composition refers to the makeup of the body, specifically the ratio or proportion of fat mass to fat-free mass (which includes muscle, bone, and water).
